ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r5.claim: The God who creates each person from a drop can recreate them; resurrection is needed so divine justice and mercy can fully appear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p68/r5.anchor: the need for it to happen is also obvious so that God’s justice and mercy can completely manifest themselves

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r1.claim: Abraham’s declaration says that God will bring him back to life after death, echoing the passage’s affirmation of resurrection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r1.anchor: who will cause me to die and then bring me back to life; who, I hope, will forgive me my sins

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.claim: With slight variations, these divine acts echo Abraham’s declaration of acquittal against his people in 26:78–82.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r2.anchor: Who has created me; then he guides me

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n35/r1.claim: The phrase literally means that the second coming to life, or resurrection, rests upon God.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n35/r1.anchor: that upon Him rests the other

QIRAAT-ER:53:47:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:47:4#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:53:47:4#1/r1.claim: The elongated nashāʾa with alif-madd and shorter nashʾa are both canonical; the longer form may stress an extended process rather than a punctual event.
QIRAAT-ER:53:47:4#1/r1.anchor: The elongated form may emphasize the process (extended duration of the act) vs the punctual event

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r1.claim: The other origination is resurrection after death, fulfilling God’s promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r1.anchor: أي الأحياء بعدالإماتة وفاءابوعده جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr says the emphasis on ‘upon Him’ addresses deniers, making resurrection sound imposed by God upon Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r2.anchor: لما كانت هذه النشأة ينكرها الكفار بولغ بقوله تعالى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says resurrection is required by wisdom so God can reward good and evil; al-Alusi questions this Muʿtazilite approach.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r3.anchor: وفي الكشاف قال سبحانه : ( عليه ) لأنها واجبة في الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr lengthen the hamza in النشأة; this remains a verbal noun of Form I نشأ.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو النشأة بالمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r7.claim: The second creation is the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p418#2/r7.anchor: أي: الخلق الثاني للبعث يوم القيامة.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r5.claim: Though known to the audience, human reproduction prepares the argument for resurrection, like 21:104; its independent evidentiary force explains the conjunction before the next clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r5.anchor: فما كان ذكره إلا تمهيدا وتوطئة لقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r6.claim: The transition is apt because the preceding verses describe how life begins, preparing for mention of the next creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p144/r6.anchor: ومناسبة الانتقال إلى هذه الجملة أن فيها كيفية ابتداء الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p147/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p147/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p147/r5.claim: Saying the next creation is upon God likens it to an assured right: divine wisdom guarantees His promise, though nothing compels God; the meaning is that He wills resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p147/r5.anchor: وفي جملة { وأن عليه النشأة } تحقيق لفعله إياها شبها بالحق الواجب على المحقوق به بحيث لا يتخلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#4/r1.claim: The second creation is the raising for resurrection on the Day of Judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#4/r1.anchor: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى وهي الخلق الثاني للبعث يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r2.claim: For an unconscious pilgrim, companions may perform the rites when customary conduct supplies consent, as though the pilgrim had spoken.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r2.anchor: قلنا: وجد الأمر منه من طريق العادة، فصار كما لو وجد نطقا

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r7.claim: The resurrection of those owed reward or compensation is incumbent, since على expresses obligation; this refutes the claim that nothing is incumbent on God.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r7.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى) على وجوب البعثة لأهل الثواب والأعواض، لأن (على) كلمة إيجاب

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r8.claim: The second creation entails that creatures first perish: what persists can only cease through an opposite or something functioning as one, so God annihilates and restores creation.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r8.anchor: وتدل على الفناء؛ لأن النشأة الثانية لا تكون إلا بعد إفناء، وما يبقى لا ينتفي إلا بضد

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r9.speaker: منهم
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r9.claim: One reported position denies that substances perish after they have come into existence.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r9.anchor: منهم من يقول: الجواهر بعد وجودها لا تفنى، وينكرون الفناء

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r10.speaker: أبو الحسين الخياط
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r10.claim: Abu al-Husayn al-Khayyat holds that God directly annihilates substances.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r10.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: يعدمها الله، وهو قول أبي الحسين الخياط

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r11.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r11.claim: Abu al-Qasim holds that substances cease because God does not create persistence in them.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r11.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: لا يخلق فيه البقاء فتنتفي، عن أبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r12.speaker: منهم
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r12.claim: Another position says God creates imperishable states in substances; when those states cease, the substances cease too.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r12.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: يخلق فيها أكوانا لا تفنى، فإذا عدمت لا يخلق فيها الأكوان، فتنتفي الجواهر

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r13.claim: The author says God restores substances by creating them again, without a distinct cause or meaning of the sort posited by rival accounts.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r13.anchor: فأما الإعادة: فعندنا يوجدها الله تعالى لا بمعنى كما أوجدها أولا

JISHUMI:v9p6665/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r14.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r14.claim: Some say the original existent comes to be by an agent, while the restored existent returns because of a cause called restoration; the author objects that this entails an infinite regress of meanings.
JISHUMI:v9p6665/r14.anchor: وعند بعضهم الموجود يوجد بإيجاد، والمعاد يعاد لعلة هي الإعادة. وقولهم يؤدي إلى تسلسل المعاني

BURSEVI:v9p209/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209/r8.claim: The other creation is resurrection after death, which God fulfills by promise; the word 'upon' does not imply an obligation imposed on God.
BURSEVI:v9p209/r8.anchor: وهو لإحياء بعد الموت وفاء بوعده لا لأنه يجب على الله

BURSEVI:v9p209/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209/r9.claim: Divine wisdom requires a second bodily creation for recompense and for believers to reach fitting perfection gradually; the world could not contain even one person's full reward, so demanding immediate results is discourteous, though a purified divine gift should be accepted and good lies in God's choice.
BURSEVI:v9p209/r9.anchor: وفيه تصريح بأن الحكمة الإلهية اقتضت النشأة الثانية الصورية للجزاء والمكافأة

BURSEVI:v9p209/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209/r10.claim: Just as bodily resurrection follows complete bodily annihilation and readiness for spirit, spiritual resurrection—subsistence and divine attributes—requires full spiritual annihilation, shedding human traits, and readiness for divine effusion.
BURSEVI:v9p209/r10.anchor: فكذا النشأة الأخرى المعنوية وهي البقاء والاتصاف بالصفات الإلهية موقوفة على تمام الفناء المعنوي

BURSEVI:v9p209/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209/r11.claim: Both resurrections require a sound constitution: a malformed embryo miscarries and a malformed womb cannot conceive; Jesus says none enters heaven's kingdom without being born twice, meaning entry into heavenly realities, lights, and secrets through the second birth of prophets and saints.
BURSEVI:v9p209/r11.anchor: وإلى الولادة الثانية التي هي النشأة الأخرى أشار عيسى عليه السلام بقوله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#10/r1.claim: The later creation is resurrection after death.

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r1.claim: Most exegetes take the other creation to mean resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r1.anchor: وهي في قول أكثر المفسرين إشارة إلى الحشر

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r2.claim: Razi proposes that the other creation may instead be the infusion of the human spirit into the embryo, joining the noble soul to a dense, dark body and honoring humanity with angel-like perception.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r2.anchor: أنه يحتمل أن يكون المراد نفخ الروح

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r3.claim: He links this spiritual creation to the other creation in 23:14: after the stages from sperm to bones, ensouling makes humans distinct from animals and is called another creation in both passages.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r3.anchor: فكسونا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا ءاخر

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r4.claim: The resurrection reading has contextual support: the preceding final destination and full recompense concern return, and 29:20 uses the phrase for resurrection; Razi answers that 29:20 mentions the beginning first, while this passage has just recalled human creation from a drop.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأن إلى ربك المنتهى } ( النجم : 42 )

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r5.claim: The spirit reading makes the sequence especially coherent: God creates male and female and gives them the human spirit, then sustains childhood through mother's milk and father's provision, and adulthood through earning; the next verse describes worldly provision.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r5.anchor: خلق الذكر والأنثى ونفخ فيهما الروح الإنسانية الشريفة

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says عليه indicates rational obligation: wise requital requires resurrection, so reason obliges God to bring it about.
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري على ما هو مذهبه عليه عقلا

RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p19#3/r7.claim: Razi rejects rational obligation on God and offers two readings: resurrection is due by God's promise, as in 36:12, or عليه means that resurrection is assigned to God as the one able to accomplish it.

RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r1.claim: One reading has النشأة as a faʿla verbal noun for a single occurrence, so the phrase means creation once more; another lengthens it as a faʿāla verbal noun. Both derive from the intransitive نشأ.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r1.anchor: على أنه مصدر كالضربة على وزن فعلة وهي للمرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r2.claim: Although الإنشاء would be the expected noun for causing something to arise, النشأة asserts that the new creation actually exists; الإنشاء could describe an attempt that produced no result.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r2.anchor: نقول فيه فائدة وهي أن الجزم يحصل

RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r3.claim: There is a nuance between creation once again, which need not presuppose a known first creation, and the other creation, which points to an already known second creation as the one due upon God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20/r3.anchor: عليه النشأة مرة أخرى لا يكون النشء قد علم أولا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#10/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#10/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#10/r1.claim: The later creation is the second creation for resurrection on the Day of Judgment.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#10/r1.anchor: أي الخلق الثاني للبعث يوم القيامة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p205/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p205/r1.claim: Both Zayd similes share the basic comparison, but كأن زيدا الأسد adds that he is so brave he is virtually indistinguishable from a lion; this extra nuance comes from the ordering and combination of the words.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p205/r1.anchor: وإنما هو زيادة فيه وفي حكم الخصوصية في الشكل

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.claim: Except verse 46, each verse in 42–50 begins wa anna, continuing the discussion of Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures in 36–41.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.anchor: Each verse in this passage, except v. 46, begins with wa anna

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.claim: Wa anna may instead be read wa inna, making each instance an independent thought meaning truly, surely, or verily.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.anchor: But wa anna could also be read wa inna, which would make each occurrence mark a new, independent thought

TABATABAI:53:43-49/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r12.claim: The second creation is the afterlife, where recompense takes place; its being incumbent on God means it is His irrevocable decree and promise, which He has said He will not break.
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r12.anchor: النشأة الأخرى الخلقة الأخرى الثانية وهي الدار الآخرة التي فيها جزاء

TABRISI:53:42-43/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:42-43/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:42-43/r4.claim: Nashʾa means fashioned, created origination, contrasted with mere willing.

TABRISI:53:44-51/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:44-51/r5.claim: The second creation is resurrection for recompense. Although ʿalā sounds like an obligation, God's promise of reward and compensation for earthly suffering entails a further life for judgment and justice, and He must fulfill His promise.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r5.anchor: فإذا لم يعوض في الدنيا وخلى بين المظلوم والظالم فلا بد من دار أخرى

THALABI:v9p156/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p156/r3.claim: The later creation is the recreation of people alive.
THALABI:v9p156/r3.anchor: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى الخلق الآخر، يعيدهم أحياء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r2.claim: The second creation is the new creation after death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r2.anchor: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى } الخلق الآخر بعد الموت

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r20.claim: God undertakes the afterlife resurrection and will deliver reward and punishment; paired creation in this world points to an afterlife.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r20.anchor: Ölümden sonraki âhiret neş’etini de O taahhüd eylemiştir; O yapacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.claim: Verses 43–49 give examples showing that all events across life and death, and all that happens in the universe, depend on God’s will and power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.anchor: insanın hayat-ölüm çizgisi içinde cereyan eden her oluşun ve evrende olup biten her şeyin Allah Teâlâ’nın irade ve kudretine bağlı bulunduğunu gösteren örnekler verilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r9.claim: The usual explanation of al-nashʾa al-ukhrā is resurrection after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r9.anchor: en-neş’etü’l-uhrâ” tamlaması genellikle “öldükten sonra diriltme” mânasıyla açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r10.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī suggests the phrase may refer to the ensoulment of the fetus, citing the preceding account of human creation and other evidence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r10.anchor: Râzî, önceki âyetlerde insanın yaratılışından söz edilmesini ve başka bazı delilleri dikkate alarak bu tamlamayla, cenine ruhun üflenmesine işaret edilmiş olabileceği kanaatine ulaştığını

ITQAN:v3p137/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r6.speaker: السهيلي
ITQAN:v3p137/r6.claim: Al-Suhayli argues the separator pronoun appears where a quality was claimed for someone besides God, as with making people laugh and weep, but not where no rival claim existed.
ITQAN:v3p137/r6.anchor: واستدل له السهيلي بأنه أتي به في كل موضع ادعي فيه نسبة ذلك المعنى إلى غير الله ولم يؤت به حيث لم يدع

MAJAZ:v2p238/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p238/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p238/r5.claim: The next creation means bringing the dead back to life.

NAHHAS:v4p278/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p278/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p278/r4.claim: God will create the pair anew after death.
NAHHAS:v4p278/r4.anchor: أي عليه أن ينشىء الزوجين بعد الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r13.claim: No emphatic هو is needed for creating the pair, the later resurrection, or destroying ʿĀd, since no one could claim these acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r13.anchor: ولما كان خلق الزوجين، والإنشاء الآخر، وإهلاك عاد ومن ذكر، لا يمكن أن يدعي ذلك أحد، لم يحتج إلى تأكيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r1.claim: The second arising is resurrection after death, which God brings about in fulfillment of His promise.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read al-nashāʾah with a long vowel; it is also a verbal noun of nashaʾa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو النشاءة بالمدة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr lengthen the hamza in “al-nashʾah”; the other readers shorten it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r7.anchor: وهو ممدود لابن كثير وأبي عمرو ومقصور لغيرهما مصدر نشأ

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r8.claim: The first creation proves the second; God’s promise makes resurrection certain because He does not change His word, not because anything is obligatory over Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r8.anchor: فلزم من ذلك الإقرار حتما بأنه قادر على البعث , عبر بما يتقضي أنه لما تقدم به وعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r3.claim: The later creation is the restoration of bodies for Resurrection after their decay in soil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r3.anchor: و: النشأة الأخرى هي إعادة الأجسام إلى الحشر بعد البلي في التراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r4.speaker: الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r4.claim: The common reading has a still shīn, hamza, and short form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الناس: «النشأة» بسكون الشين والهمز والقصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو والأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿraj read the word with a long vowel.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r4.claim: The One who created people initially is able to bring them back in the afterlife on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: {وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى} أي: كما خلق البداءة هو قادر على الإعادة، وهي النشأة الآخرة يوم القيامة.

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r12.claim: Nashʾa is a newly made creation; the two creations are initial life and resurrection.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r12.anchor: والنشأة: الصنعة المخترعة، أنشأ ينشيء إنشاء: إذا ابتدع، وهما نشأتان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r15.claim: النشأة is also read النشاءة with a long vowel.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r16.claim: The next creation is incumbent on God by wisdom so that good and evil can be recompensed.

MUQATIL:53:43-50/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r5.claim: The other creation is resurrection after death in the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r5.anchor: يعني الخلق الآخر يعني البعث في الآخرة بعد الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r1.claim: The second creation means restoring spirits to bodies for resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r1.anchor: أي إعادة الأرواح في الأشباح للبعث

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read nashʾa with an open sh and lengthened vowel; it refers to the promised resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «النشأة» بفتح الشين والمد

NASHR:v2p343/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r3.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p343/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read النشأة with an alif after the shin in al-Ankabut, al-Najm, and al-Waqia.
NASHR:v2p343/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في الثلاثة بألف بعد الشين

NASHR:v2p343/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r4.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p343/r4.claim: The remaining readers omit the alif after shin in these three occurrences.
NASHR:v2p343/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بإسكان الشين من غير ألف فيها
